rows.note: I assumed "support rep" refers to the Customer.SupportRepId column, and that full name means first name followed by last name.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count
FROM (
    SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_purchase
    FROM Invoice
    GROUP BY CustomerId
) AS first_purchases
WHERE strftime('%Y', first_purchase) = '2010';
rows.note: I assumed a customer's "very first purchase" is their earliest invoice date across all time, counted if that date falls in 2010.

rows.sql:
SELECT a."Title", ROUND(SUM(t."Milliseconds") / 60000.0, 1) AS "TotalMinutes"
FROM "Album" a
JOIN "Track" t ON t."AlbumId" = a."AlbumId"
GROUP BY a."AlbumId", a."Title"
ORDER BY SUM(t."Milliseconds") DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed total running time is the sum of track `Milliseconds` per album, converted to minutes (divided by 60,000).

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS Year,
         SUM(Total) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY Year
)
SELECT Year,
       ROUND((Revenue - LAG(Revenue) OVER (ORDER BY Year)) * 100.0 / LAG(Revenue) OVER (ORDER BY Year), 1) AS YoYPctChange
FROM yearly
ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: I assumed revenue means the sum of `Total` from the Invoice table, grouped by calendar year of `InvoiceDate`. The first year is shown with NULL since it has no prior year to compare against.

rows.sql:
WITH customer_spend AS (
    SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spent
    FROM Invoice
    GROUP BY CustomerId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_average
FROM customer_spend
WHERE spent > (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM customer_spend);
rows.note: I assumed the average is taken only over customers who have at least one invoice.

rows.sql:
SELECT p.Name
FROM Playlist p
JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed artists are linked to tracks through their album, so tracks without an album are not counted, and ties are broken arbitrarily.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count
FROM (
    SELECT il.InvoiceId
    FROM InvoiceLine il
    JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
    GROUP BY il.InvoiceId
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1
) AS multi_genre_invoices;
rows.note: Assumption: tracks with a NULL GenreId are not counted as a separate genre.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS SupportRepFullName,
       SUM(i.Total) AS TotalRevenue2010
FROM Invoice i
JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
WHERE strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2010'
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName
ORDER BY TotalRevenue2010 DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed "support rep" means the employee linked to each customer through `Customer.SupportRepId`, and that revenue is the sum of `Invoice.Total`.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_orders
FROM Orders
WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
  AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate;
rows.note: I assumed orders with no ShippedDate (not yet shipped) should be excluded from the count.
I assumed "shipped orders" means orders with a non-null ShippedDate.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count
FROM Products
WHERE Discontinued = '0'
  AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel;
rows.note:
Discontinued is stored as TEXT with default '0', so "not discontinued" means Discontinued = '0'.



I assumed "not discontinued" corresponds to the value '0' in the Discontinued column.

rows.sql:
SELECT c.Country, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount
FROM Orders o
JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2019'
GROUP BY c.Country
ORDER BY OrderCount DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I assumed "placed the most orders" means counting orders by the customer's country (from the Customers table) for orders dated in 2019.

rows.sql:
SELECT ROUND(
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages'
                   THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END)
  / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)),
  1) AS beverages_pct_of_2023_revenue
FROM "Order Details" od
JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2023';
rows.note: Assumption: "2023" refers to the year of OrderDate, and revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount). The sample order dates are from 2016–2018, so this may return NULL if no 2023 orders exist.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count
FROM (
    SELECT CustomerID
    FROM Orders
    WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01'
    GROUP BY CustomerID
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12
) AS yearly_customers;
rows.note: I assumed "every month" means all 12 calendar months of 2020 based on `OrderDate`, so the result may be 0 if the data has no 2020 orders.

rows.sql:
WITH order_values AS (
    SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID,
           SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS val
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
    GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName,
       AVG(ov.val) AS AvgOrderValue
FROM order_values ov
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ov.EmployeeID
GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
ORDER BY AvgOrderValue DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumes orders without any line items are excluded, since they have no value to average.

rows.sql:
SELECT s.CompanyName,
       SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue
FROM "Order Details" od
JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018'
GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName
ORDER BY Revenue DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumes revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from the order line items, with 2018 determined by the order date.
